# M4 wiring: ESP32-S3 + 2× TB6612FNG + hardware dead-man + INA226

**Status: draft, nothing assembled or powered.** Schematic: [`wiring.kicad_sch`](wiring.kicad_sch), generated by [`tools/gen_wiring.py`](tools/gen_wiring.py) (edit the generator, not the schematic; `--check` compares KiCad's netlist with the intended nets). Nets join by label name. Validated: ERC 0 errors (only the expected embedded-library warnings), `scripts/check-kicad-labels.py` clean, netlist equal to intent (35 nets).

Pin numbers `Lnn`/`Rnn` are physical header positions of the boards in hand, as in M1 and [`docs/reference/`](../../docs/reference/). Every number marked *placeholder* waits for the bench ([TESTPLAN.md](TESTPLAN.md)).

## Signal map

M1's four pins are kept (GPIO4/5/6/7, bench-proven on channel A). The rest are free header pins the board doc allows: no strapping pins (0, 3, 45, 46), no PSRAM pins (35-37), no USB pins (19-21), not GPIO48 (RGB LED, still the indicator), not UART0 (43/44: logs and bench commands).

| Net | ESP32-S3 GPIO (header) | Goes to | Role |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `STBY_EN` | **4** (L4) | 74HC123 `~1RD` (pin 3), 10 kΩ to GND | Firmware's enable request |
| `D1_AIN1` / `D1_AIN2` / `D1_PWMA` | **5 / 6 / 7** (L5/L6/L7) | D1 `AIN1` R3 / `AIN2` R2 / `PWMA` R1 | Channel D1A (M1's channel) |
| `D1_PWMB` / `D1_BIN1` / `D1_BIN2` | 15 / 16 / 17 (L8/L9/L10) | D1 `PWMB` R7 / `BIN1` R5 / `BIN2` R6 | Channel D1B |
| `D2_PWMA` / `D2_AIN1` / `D2_AIN2` | 8 / 9 / 10 (L12/L15/L16) | D2 `PWMA` R1 / `AIN1` R3 / `AIN2` R2 | Channel D2A |
| `D2_PWMB` / `D2_BIN1` / `D2_BIN2` | 11 / 12 / 13 (L17/L18/L19) | D2 `PWMB` R7 / `BIN1` R5 / `BIN2` R6 | Channel D2B |
| `HEARTBEAT` | 14 (L20) | 74HC123 `1B` (pin 2), 10 kΩ to GND | Toggled by the control tick only |
| `STBY` | 39 (R9), input | 74HC123 `1Q` (pin 13) → D1 `STBY` R4, D2 `STBY` R4, 10 kΩ to GND | Both drivers' standby, read back |
| `SDA` / `SCL` | 1 / 2 (R4/R5) | INA226 module | I²C, 400 kHz |
| `INA_ALERT` | 38 (R10), input, pull-up | INA226 `ALERT` (open-drain) | Wired, not used by the draft yet |
| `ESP_RST` | `RST` (L3) | logic analyzer only | Shows watchdog resets |

PWM: MCPWM0, 20 kHz (M1's frequency; TB6612 max 100 kHz), 1000 steps. D1A/D1B on operator 0, D2A/D2B on operator 1, one timer. Wheel to channel mapping is a placeholder (FL = D1A, RL = D1B, FR = D2A, RR = D2B; O8, M5) and lives in `Config::BENCH`, not in the wiring.

Why these pins are safe at reset (SoC datasheet, pin table and Table 2-2): GPIO4-8 come out of reset with no pull and input disabled, 9-14 input only; GPIO1-14 and 17 can show a 60 µs **low** glitch at power-up, which cannot enable a driver. GPIO18 shows a **high** glitch, so it is left unused. GPIO38/39 are inputs only here.

## Power

```text
Bench PSU + ── F1 fuse ── SW1 kill switch ── INA226 IN+ ═shunt═ IN- ── VM ──┬── D1 VM (L1) ── C1 bulk
                                                                             └── D2 VM (L1) ── C2 bulk
Bench PSU − ── GND ── D1/D2 GND ── ESP32 GND ── INA226 GND ── 74HC123 GND ── logic analyzer GND
ESP32 3V3 (L1/L2) ── D1/D2 VCC (L2), 74HC123 VCC (16) + 100 nF, INA226 VCC
ESP32 power: USB-C from the laptop on the COM (CH343) port only; nothing on 5Vin.
```

* **VM range:** TB6612FNG operating range 4.5-13.5 V; **1.0 A per channel only at VM ≥ 5 V, 0.4 A between 4.5 and 5 V**; absolute 1.2 A average, 3.2 A for a single 10 ms pulse. A 5 V source that sags below 5 V under load cuts the allowed current to 0.4 A.
* **Motor voltage:** unknown (TT motors, no datasheet; see [mecanum reference](../../docs/reference/mecanum-car/README.md)). Start at 5.0 V, current-limited; only M1's 5 V power bank point exists so far.
* **PSU current limit** (placeholder): 0.5 A for one motor, raised per TESTPLAN step. It is the first protection; F1 and SW1 are the second and the manual stop.
* **C1/C2 bulk caps** (placeholder 470 µF, ≥ 16 V, at each driver's VM): the breakout boards' own capacitors are unknown. **C3-C6** 100 nF ceramic across each motor's terminals, if the motors have none.
* **Common ground** is required (as M1). Do not feed 5 V into `3V3`; it is the board regulator's output (M1 WIRING).

### INA226 on the rail

High side, between the kill switch and both drivers' VM, so it sees the whole motor current. VBUS goes to the load side (VM). Address 0x40 (A0 = A1 = GND). The firmware uses the power-on configuration (continuous, 1.1 ms conversions, no averaging; register 00h = 4127h) and reads shunt (01h) and bus (02h) registers every 10 ms tick.

**Shunt range:** INA226 full scale is ±81.92 mV. Common modules carry a 0.1 Ω (`R100`) shunt: **±0.82 A only**, too little for four motors starting together. Buy or fit a 0.01 Ω (`R010`, ±8.2 A) shunt and set `SHUNT_MILLIOHM` in `firmware/src/fw.rs`. Peaks shorter than one 1.1 ms conversion are averaged away; it is a rail logger, not a scope.

## Fail-safe: motors stop when the firmware hangs

This is M4's acceptance question. TB6612FNG facts it rests on: `STBY` low puts both channels' outputs Hi-Z; each input has an internal 200 kΩ pull-down.

| # | Option | Covers a hang that keeps `STBY_EN` high? | Cost / risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | Software only: core watchdog plus the chip's RTC watchdog; reset floats the GPIOs and the TB6612's 200 kΩ pull-down holds standby | Only after the RTC watchdog fires (placeholder 1 s), and only if nothing keeps feeding it | No parts. Weak pull-down next to motor wiring |
| B | A + 10 kΩ external pull-downs on `STBY_EN` / `STBY` | Same as A | Three resistors; fixes the weak pull-down and the "ESP unpowered" case |
| **C** | **B + a retriggerable monostable (74HC123) as a dead-man: `STBY = 1Q`, high only while `STBY_EN` is high and the control tick keeps toggling `HEARTBEAT`** | **Yes, within `tw` (placeholder ~110 ms), whatever level the pins freeze at** | One DIP-16 chip, an R and a C; `tw` is set by parts and must be measured |
| D | B + an external supervisor IC (e.g. TPS3823-class watchdog) pulling reset or `STBY` | Yes | SMD parts, needs a breakout; one more thing to source |
| E | Cut VM with a MOSFET or relay from the same dead-man | Yes, and also a driver that fails shorted | High-current switching, inductive kickback; car-level, later |
| F | Charge pump (AC-coupled heartbeat, diodes, RC) into a Schmitt gate | Yes | Passives and a 74HC14/132; harder to reason about than C |

**Recommendation: C, with B's pull-downs and A's RTC watchdog kept as layers, plus the PSU limit, F1 and SW1 on the bench.** Reasons: it is the only cheap breadboard option that is independent of the firmware's state; a frozen pin (high or low) stops the edges, so it covers stuck loops, a dead executor, a panic and a hold in reset; the clear input gives the AND with `STBY_EN` in the same chip, so there is no extra gate. The heartbeat must come from a GPIO the control tick toggles in code, never from a PWM or other peripheral that keeps running on its own when the CPU hangs.

How C behaves (74HC123 function table, Nexperia datasheet):

| Condition | `~1RD` (`STBY_EN`) | `1B` (`HEARTBEAT`) | `STBY` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ESP32 unpowered, in reset, booting | low (R1) | floating → low (R2) | **low** |
| Firmware standby (core says so) | low | toggling | **low** |
| Enabled, tick running | high | rising edge every 20 ms | high (retriggered before `tw` ends) |
| Hang with pins frozen high or low | either | no edges | **low after `tw`** |
| Hang, then RTC watchdog reset | floats → low | floats → low | low; reset cause logged at boot |

* `tw = K × Rext × Cext`; K is 0.45 at 5 V and 0.55 at 2 V (datasheet Fig. 6), so about 0.5 at 3.3 V: 220 kΩ × 1 µF → **~110 ms, placeholder**. It must be longer than two ticks plus jitter (20 ms + margin) and as short as the O4 bound allows. Use a ceramic Cext (no polarity); Rext must stay within 2 kΩ-1 MΩ.
* A rising edge on `~1RD` with `1B` high can start one `tw` pulse (function table). That only happens when the firmware raises `STBY_EN`, i.e. on purpose; without further heartbeat edges it ends after `tw`.
* Unused half: `~2RD`, `2A`, `2B` to GND; outputs and RC pins open.
* Optional later: INA226 `ALERT` (open-drain) could also pull the `~1RD` node low through the same net for a hardware over-current stop. That needs a series resistor from GPIO4 so the open-drain output can win; not in this draft.

## Logic-analyzer probe list

8 channels, 24 MHz, `sigrok-cli` (fx2lafw). **Inputs are 5 V max: never probe `AO*`/`BO*` motor outputs or VM.** Clip ground to ESP32 GND, one point.

| Ch | Capture A: fail-safe (schematic J1) | Capture B: four channels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| D0 | `STBY_EN` (GPIO4) | `STBY` |
| D1 | `HEARTBEAT` (GPIO14) | `D1_PWMA` (GPIO7) |
| D2 | `STBY` (74HC123 1Q / driver R4) | `D1_PWMB` (GPIO15) |
| D3 | `D1_PWMA` (GPIO7) | `D2_PWMA` (GPIO8) |
| D4 | `D1_AIN1` (GPIO5) | `D2_PWMB` (GPIO11) |
| D5 | `D1_AIN2` (GPIO6) | `HEARTBEAT` |
| D6 | `INA_ALERT` (GPIO38) | `D2_AIN1` (GPIO9) |
| D7 | `ESP_RST` (L3) | `D2_AIN2` (GPIO10) |

Sample at ≥ 4 MHz (20 kHz PWM, 50 µs period). Example, untried: `sigrok-cli -d fx2lafw -c samplerate=4m --time 3000 -t D2=f -w -o bench/<run>/stby.sr` (trigger on `STBY` falling).

## Assumptions to verify on the bench

1. INA226 module pinout, shunt value and whether VBUS is tied to IN- on the board: **not bought yet**; its symbol is numbered by function, not by header.
2. 74HC123 DIP-16 pin numbers come from the Nexperia datasheet; check the TI CD74HC123E datasheet (same standard pinout) for the part actually bought.
3. The TB6612 breakouts' on-board components (VM capacitor, pull-ups) are unknown; the reference only documents the headers.
4. GPIO38/39 assumed free and 3.3 V on this board (plain GPIO on the header); GPIO39-42 are the pad JTAG pins, which stay unused while JTAG goes over USB (eFuse default, not checked).
5. `IN1 = IN2 = L` with PWM low is not a row in the transcribed truth table (only PWM high is listed as Stop); the firmware uses it for coast and standby. TESTPLAN T2 checks the outputs really are off.
6. The 74HC123 `tw` at 3.3 V and the RC values: measured in TESTPLAN T3.
